import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Fill NaN in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'None' for clarity
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Define a logical order for BMI Category for better visualization
bmi_order = ['Normal', 'Overweight', 'Obese']
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=bmi_order, ordered=True)

# Define a logical order for the columns in the plot
disorder_order = ['None', 'Insomnia', 'Sleep Apnea']

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create a faceted scatter plot using relplot
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x="Stress Level",
    y="Quality of Sleep",
    hue="BMI Category",
    size="Physical Activity Level",
    col="Sleep Disorder",
    kind="scatter",
    palette="plasma",
    sizes=(30, 350),
    alpha=0.8,
    height=6.5,
    aspect=1,
    hue_order=bmi_order,
    col_order=disorder_order
)

# --- Customization and Titling ---
# Set custom axis labels
g.set_axis_labels("Stress Level (1-10)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)", fontsize=14)

# Set individual facet titles
g.set_titles("Sleep Disorder: {col_name}", size=16)

# Add a clear, descriptive main title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle(
    "Interplay of Stress, BMI, and Activity on Sleep Quality",
    fontsize=22,
    y=1.03, # Adjust title vertical position
    fontweight='bold'
)

# Improve the legend title and placement
g.legend.set_title("BMI Category", prop={'size': 14, 'weight': 'bold'})
plt.setp(g.legend.get_texts(), fontsize='12')

# Adjust layout to prevent title overlap
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
